subject: salt shaker
title: What If You Never Ate Salt Again?

scenes.text: What if you never added salt again? Your body would barely notice, until you started sweating.
Your body needs less than 500 milligrams of sodium a day. Plain food already contains some.
Your kidneys hold on to it tightly. The Yanomami of the Amazon eat almost no salt, and their blood pressure stays low for life.
The danger is sweat. Every liter can carry away up to two grams of sodium.
Lose too much in heat or illness, and blood sodium drops below 135. Headaches, confusion, cramps, even seizures.
So skipping the salt shaker is fine. Running out of sodium is what hurts.

description:
What if you never ate salt? The body needs less than 500 mg of sodium a day and healthy kidneys conserve it; the Yanomami, with one of the lowest salt intakes ever measured, keep a blood pressure around 95/61 that does not rise with age.
The real risk is losing sodium through heavy sweating or illness: sweat carries roughly 0.2 to 2 g per liter, and blood sodium below 135 mmol/L (hyponatremia) causes headaches, confusion, cramps and in severe cases seizures. Not medical advice.
